learningObjectives.statement: Identify major vehicle systems and explain their basic functional relationships without treating a system overview as a vehicle-specific service procedure.
Distinguish a customer concern, observation, measurement, technical reference, hypothesis, and diagnostic conclusion.
Use safety, professional practice, and applicable technical information to select and document an appropriate next step for a basic vehicle concern.

contentBlocks.title: What learners already know

contentBlocks.title: Technical information and source boundary
contentBlocks.description: Reinforce that vehicle-specific procedures, specifications, limits, and safety instructions require applicable authoritative information.

lessonContentPlans.lessonSummary: Develop a disciplined approach to automotive shop safety, hazardous-material and environmental awareness, tool and equipment boundaries, high-voltage hazard recognition, documentation, and professional responsibility without substituting generic instruction for applicable site, product, vehicle, or regulatory requirements.

learningObjectives.statement: Identify common categories of automotive shop hazards and distinguish hazard recognition from authorization to perform a specific task.
Use applicable safety, environmental, equipment, product, and technical information to determine whether work may proceed, requires additional controls, or should stop and be escalated.
Document observed hazards, selected controls, professional communication, and the reason for a safe next action without inventing limits, procedures, or regulatory requirements.

contentBlocks.title: Lesson targets
contentBlocks.description: Preview the hazard-recognition, information-use, documentation, and professional-decision outcomes for the lesson.

contentBlocks.title: Safety starts before the task
contentBlocks.description: Connect prior shop experience to the principle that recognizing a task is not the same as being authorized, equipped, or informed to perform it.

contentBlocks.title: Hazard categories in automotive work
contentBlocks.description: Organize hazards around work areas, materials, tools and equipment, electrical or stored energy, and environmental conditions without assigning universal thresholds.

contentBlocks.title: Recognize, verify, control, document, escalate
contentBlocks.description: Use a conceptual process model for moving from a recognized hazard to an information-supported professional action.

contentBlocks.title: When the safest next step is to stop
contentBlocks.description: Demonstrate how an unclear hazard, missing information, or uncertain authorization can lead to a documented stop-work and escalation decision rather than an improvised procedure.

contentBlocks.title: Hazard and information sorting
contentBlocks.description: Classify sample observations by hazard category and identify what applicable information would be needed before proceeding.

contentBlocks.title: Safe next-action scenario
contentBlocks.description: Select whether to proceed, add controls, stop, or escalate in a generalized shop scenario and justify the decision using the information available.

contentBlocks.title: Safety reasoning check

contentBlocks.title: Explain the safer choice and retry
contentBlocks.description: Provide reasoning-focused feedback and allow revision without creating scored assessment eligibility.

contentBlocks.title: Applicable information governs the task
contentBlocks.description: Reinforce that site rules, product information, equipment instructions, vehicle-specific information, and applicable legal or regulatory requirements must be verified rather than invented.

contentBlocks.title: Professional safety practice summary
contentBlocks.description: Summarize hazard recognition, information use, controls, documentation, stop-work authority, escalation, and professional communication as foundations for later technical work.
